_comment: You do not need this file any more: the Servers pane adds, switches on
and removes servers for you, and writes mcp.json itself. This is here for
anyone who would rather edit it by hand, and to document the shape - which
is the one every other MCP client uses, so a config pastes in from
elsewhere.
A server is reached one of two ways, and the entry says which: a command,
started here as a subprocess, or a url, reached over Streamable HTTP. One
or the other - an entry carrying both does not say which was meant, so it
is skipped rather than guessed at.
A credential goes in an env block for a command server, or a headers block
for a url one. Either the value itself, or "${VAR}", which is read from
the environment so the secret never lands in this file. Only a value that
is entirely ${VAR} expands - "Bearer ${VAR}" is sent literally, so put
the whole header value in the variable, Bearer included. Keep mcp.json out
of version control either way; the .gitignore already does.
Sign-in that needs a browser (interactive OAuth) is not supported. A server
wanting it answers 401, and the error says so.
Nothing here runs until you run POST /api/mcp/refresh once: the tool list
is cached, because the registry is rebuilt every turn and starting a
subprocess per server each time is not affordable on this machine. After
a refresh, a server starts only when one of its tools is actually called,
and is stopped again after mcp_idle_timeout.
A tool the server annotates with readOnlyHint runs freely. Everything
else is shown to you for approval first, the way `git commit` and a POST
are. Set "trusted": true on a server to skip that for all of its tools -
which is a thing to state deliberately, not a default.
Each server is its own lens category (mcp:<name>), so its schemas stay
out of the prompt until the conversation looks like it needs them.
